note: Cycle-2 mining: candidates the miners themselves killed during pre-proposal verification (2026-08-20), each with the kill pattern and fetched evidence. The seven kill patterns are defined in research/CYCLE2_BALLOT.md and PLAN.md.

rejected.name: CostReport Press — Medicare cost report (CMS-2552-10 / CAH) generator from trial balance + statistics
rejected.killed_by: Regulatory gate that an unattended startup cannot clear (hard variant of pattern 3), compounded by pattern 7
rejected.evidence: The electronic cost report file cannot legally be produced by arbitrary software. First Coast Service Options (the MAC) states the provider must submit 'The electronic cost report (ECR) and print image (PI) files utilizing CMS-approved vendor with current specification date' — https://medicare.fcso.com/cost-reporting/electronic-submission-supporting-documentation, fetched 2026-08-20. CMS's MCReF page and Noridian's guidance point to the same ECR-software path (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/audits-compliance/part-a-cost-report/medicare-cost-report-electronic-filing-mcref, fetched 2026-08-20). Becoming a CMS-certified ECR vendor is a human-in-the-loop certification process, which fails A1/A6 before the product exists. Separately, cost-report preparation turns on cost-allocation choices (statistics bases, stepdown order, related-party adjustments) that are judgement, not arithmetic — the AI would be arbiter, not engine. Dead on both counts.

rejected.name: PAMA Lab — CLFS private payor rate and volume reporting file for applicable laboratories
rejected.killed_by: Not recurring in any usable window (fails the 'mandatory RECURRING' premise); timing already passed
rejected.evidence: CMS's own CLFS/PAMA reporting page (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-schedules/clinical-laboratory-fee-schedule/clfs-pama-reporting-resources, fetched 2026-08-20) shows the data collection period was 1 Jan – 30 Jun 2025 and the data reporting period ran 1 May – 31 Jul 2026 — closed three weeks ago. Section 6226 of the CAA 2026, enacted 3 February 2026, again reset the reporting requirements and the phase-in ('no phase-in reduction in 2026; beginning January 1, 2027 – 2029, payment may not be reduced by more than 15% per year'). Reporting is triennial and has been statutorily delayed repeatedly, so the next artifact is years out and its existence depends on Congress. The underlying computation (weighted median private payor rate and volume per HCPCS from the lab's own remittances) is a perfect fit for the engine — but there is nothing to generate for roughly two and a half years, and a product whose next billable event is a Congressional decision is not a subscription.

rejected.name: HPT TXT — cms-hpt.txt and MRF file-naming compliance product
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1: free first-party generator already exists
rejected.evidence: CMS itself ships both artifacts as free web tools: the TXT File Generator at https://cmsgov.github.io/hpt-tool/txt-generator/ and the MRF File Name Wizard at https://cmsgov.github.io/hpt-tool/filename-wizard/ (both surfaced and confirmed 2026-08-20, and named as such in CMS's own repo README fetched the same day: 'a MRF File Naming Wizard, a TXT File Generator, and a Validator V2.0'). These are the only two parts of the §180 obligation CMS has automated for hospitals — which is precisely why they are the parts nobody can sell, and why the generator opportunity sits in the file CMS did not automate. Survives only as a free giveaway feature inside ChargeFile.

rejected.name: Shoppable300 — standalone generator for the §180.60 consumer-friendly display of 300 shoppable services
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1/2: a free third-party substitute is already in market and includes hosting
rejected.evidence: Craneware's Trisus Pricing Transparency page states 'Available at no cost to all US healthcare providers, Trisus Pricing Transparency helps you meet the requirements of the rule' and 'Craneware also offers a hosting option, providing a user-friendly website for your patients to search services. Again, this offering is free to every U.S. healthcare provider owning or managing acute care hospitals' (page text pulled directly 2026-08-20 from https://www.thecranewaregroup.com/solutions/pricing/trisus-pricing-transparency/). A free, hosted, patient-facing shoppable-services site from a listed vendor is exactly the substitute that kills a paid standalone. It does not kill the MRF generator — the same page contains no occurrence of 'machine-readable', 'v3.0', 'allowed amount', 'percentile', 'attestation' or '2026' — so the shoppable display is kept as a bundled tier of ChargeFile, never as a company.

rejected.name: MRF Lake — aggregating and reselling hospital price-transparency data
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2/3: the category is saturated by funded incumbents who already ingest everything
rejected.evidence: Payerset states it ingests '100% of published machine-readable files' and sells Rate Explorer plus a Data Lake (https://www.payerset.com/pricing, fetched 2026-08-20). Turquoise Health's provider page advertises search across 'hospital and payer-negotiated rates pulled directly from machine-readable files with full traceability to the source' and identifies itself as a CMS Qualified Entity (https://turquoise.health/for_providers, fetched 2026-08-20), and announced a $40M Series C led by Oak HC/FT in March 2026. Serif Health and Mathematica occupy the same shelf. This is the demand side of the same regulation, and it is fully served. The unserved side is supply: producing the file, not consuming it.

rejected.name: LeakLedger — EPA 40 CFR Part 84 refrigerant leak-rate logs and the HFC Chronic Leak Report (Form 3520-36)
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2 (live micro-SaaS incumbent, with a FREE tier doing exactly this) — and this was the angle's most promising lead, with a genuine new mandate and a real spec gap.
rejected.evidence: The mandate is real and fresh: 40 CFR Part 84 Subpart C applies as of 1 January 2026, an appliance holding 15+ lb that leaks 125%+ of full charge in a calendar year is a 'chronically leaking appliance', and the first reports are due to EPA 1 March 2027. EPA publishes the SPEC but not a generator — I downloaded its Excel form 'HFC Chronic Leak Report 3520-36' (https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2026-02/hfc-chronic-leak-report-3520-36.xlsx, HTTP 200, 120,504 bytes, fetched 2026-08-20) from https://www.epa.gov/climate-hfcs-reduction/reporting-resources-emissions-reduction-reclamation-rule (fetched 2026-08-20), which lists seven Excel forms and a Leak Reporting User Guide and no calculator. Then the market check killed it: RefriTrak (https://www.refritrak.com/en/pricing, fetched 2026-08-20) already ships '40 CFR Part 84 Subpart C tracking', 'Automated EPA leak rate calculations' and 'Chronic leaker detection & alerts' on a FREE forever plan (500 entries/month, 2 users), with Professional at $15/seat/month annual. A free tier doing the exact deterministic computation is an unbeatable floor. The space is additionally crowded — RefriComply, Facilio and Fexa Trakref all publish 2026 Subpart C comparison content. Not proposed.

rejected.name: CCR Composer — annual Consumer Confidence Report generation for community water systems
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 (free first-party GENERATOR, live today) — the clean case: EPA does not merely publish a template, it hosts an application that produces the finished artifact.
rejected.evidence: EPA's CCR iWriter is live and self-describing. I fetched https://ofmpub.epa.gov/apex/safewater/f?p=140:LOGIN_DESKTOP on 2026-08-20 (HTTP 200, 22,990 bytes); the page reads 'CCR iWriter — This application enables you to produce a regulation compliant Consumer Confidence Report (CCR)' and offers free self-signup. The mandate and the trigger were otherwise excellent — the CCR Rule Revisions final rule (Federal Register, May 2024) has a first compliance date of 1 January 2027 with biannual delivery for systems serving over 10,000, and the mandatory verbatim health-effects language sits in 40 CFR 141 Subpart O Appendix A, i.e. machine-readable via the eCFR API. None of that survives a free federal generator aimed at the same ~49,000 community water systems. Not proposed.

rejected.name: ManifestMaker — RCRA hazardous waste e-Manifest generation
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 and 3 together: EPA runs the free system AND publishes a free developer API, and the receiving facility/transporter already prepares the form as part of the disposal service.
rejected.evidence: https://www.epa.gov/e-manifest (fetched 2026-08-20, page last updated 2026-07-31) confirms EPA provides the electronic manifest system through RCRAInfo, links 'Developer Documentation' on GitHub for programmatic access, and notes EPA-set user fees for FY2026–2027. When the agency operates both the UI and the API for the artifact, and the waste vendor fills it in as part of the haul, there is no generator gap. Not proposed.

rejected.name: FormR Assembler — TRI Form R preparation for small manufacturers
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 (EPA's free TRI-MEweb completes and submits the form), compounded by kill pattern 7 (release estimation is engineering judgment, not deterministic arithmetic).
rejected.evidence: https://www.epa.gov/toxics-release-inventory-tri-program/electronic-submission-tri-reporting-forms (fetched 2026-08-20, last updated 2026-07-06) states TRI-MEweb 'guides facility representatives through the process of completing, reviewing, and submitting TRI reporting forms' — first-party preparation plus submission for the same annual 1 July filing. The residual value would be estimating release quantities from throughput, which requires emission factors and engineering judgment the AI must not sign, and commercial TRI software already exists (ERA Environmental). Not proposed.

rejected.name: Superfund Chemical Excise Tax generator (IRS Form 6627 / Form 720)
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 in an unusual form — the government form IS the calculator — plus kill pattern 7 on the upstream step that actually carries the value.
rejected.evidence: The mandate is alive and recurring: IRS's Superfund chemical excise taxes page (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/superfund-chemical-excise-taxes, fetched 2026-08-20, page last updated 2026-08-17) confirms quarterly Form 720 plus Form 6627 with semimonthly EFTPS deposits, and the taxable-substances list is actively maintained (Federal Register notice of 2026-06-26 adding substances effective 2026-01-01; Form 6627 instructions revised January 2026). But Form 6627 is itself a rate-times-tons worksheet with the published rate printed on the form, so 'generation' adds nothing. The genuine work — mapping an importer's customs/HTS lines to CAS-identified taxable substances and deriving tons — is not deterministic (customs data does not carry CAS numbers; the fallback is 10% of appraised entry value precisely because conversion factors are unknowable), which puts a signed tax liability on judgment the engine must not exercise. Soft, so not proposed.

rejected.name: SWPPP inspection log generator (industrial/construction stormwater) and RCRA Biennial Report
rejected.killed_by: SWPPP: kill pattern 4 (no submitted artifact — inspection logs are retained on site, and their content lives in per-state general-permit prose, which is also a kill pattern 5 conflict). Biennial Report: cadence — the artifact is filed in even years by 1 March, so the next filing after March 2026 is March 2028, 18 months out.
rejected.evidence: For the stormwater family generally, EPA has built free NeT modules that occupy the submission channel — EPA's reporting-tool posture is visible on https://www.epa.gov/compliance/npdes-ereporting (fetched 2026-08-20), which describes Phase 2 electronic reporting (extended to 21 December 2025) covering NOIs, MS4 Program Reports and CAFO Annual Reports through EPA-provided tools. Honest caveat on the Biennial Report: I could not fetch a primary EPA page today (https://www.epa.gov/hwgenerators/hazardous-waste-biennial-report returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-20), so this rejection rests on filing cadence rather than on a source I fetched, and should be re-checked if the angle is revisited. Not proposed.

rejected.name: Form 13F information-table generator (holdings CSV + SEC official 13(f) securities list to EDGAR XML)
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 2 — live micro-SaaS incumbent already doing exactly this, cheaper than the imagined price
rejected.evidence: The premise checked out: SEC's own Form 13F FAQ (https://www.sec.gov/divisions/investment/13ffaq, fetched 2026-08-20) confirms filers must 'construct the Information Table according to the EDGAR XML Technical Specification' and that SEC ships no software ('EDGARlink software was retired on September 12, 2011'), and that the Official List of 13(f) securities became available in .txt as well as .pdf 'Beginning with 4Q 2025'. But the exact product exists: Advanced Computer Innovations' 13F portal (https://web.acii.com/13f.htm, fetched 2026-08-20) takes an Excel holdings upload with only CUSIP/Quantity/Value required, states 'No need to aggregate, scrub or filter holdings against the SEC 13-F list - this service does it all for you', and prices at 'The price is $100 plus 0.1 to 10 cents per input line... A filing with up to 250 entries costs $100 to $125', free preview, pay on download. File13F additionally advertises full-service filing at $175/quarter (search-level, 2026-08-20). Nothing left to wedge.

rejected.name: HMDA LAR file generator for small lenders
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 1 — the agency ships two free generators, not just a validator
rejected.evidence: CFPB's Excel LAR Formatting Tool page (https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/tools/lar-formatting/, fetched 2026-08-20): users enter transmittal and loan-level data, click 'Create LAR File', and 'The data is now formatted into a pipe delimited text file (as shown below) and ready to be submitted to the HMDA Platform.' Free, on the CFPB/FFIEC site. A second free Online LAR Formatting Tool does the same entirely in-browser. The free HMDA Platform then validates. The generator half — the only part worth selling — is already given away by the regulator.

rejected.name: FEC Form 3/3X .fec file generator for small campaign committees
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 1 — free first-party filing software from the agency
rejected.evidence: FEC's own page (https://www.fec.gov/help-candidates-and-committees/filing-reports/electronic-filing/getting-started-fecfile-plus/, fetched 2026-08-20): 'FECfile+, the new web-based version of FECFile, is the free electronic filing software for committees' that lets 'filers create, review and submit reports from anywhere on both Macs and PCs'. Rollout is currently limited ('only newly registered PACs that do not allocate or who have not registered as a lobbyist/registrant can use FECfile+') but the legacy FECFile desktop remains free and the FEC also publishes the .fec format spec and a list of approved third-party vendors. The agency both generates and files, for free.

rejected.name: NMLS Mortgage Call Report (MCR FV7) generator for small mortgage brokers and lenders
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 3 — already bundled inside the loan origination system the buyer pays for
rejected.evidence: The mandate and spec are real and freshly versioned (MCR Form Version 7 required from Q1 2026, XSD published 2025-10-31, first FV7 filing due 2026-05-15 — search-level via Orrick InfoBytes, 2026-08-20). But the job is done free inside the LOS: LendingPad's knowledge base (https://kb.lendingpad.com/how-to-file-nmls-call-report-mcr, fetched 2026-08-20) walks users through Reports > 'NMLS Mortgage Call Report (MCR)' > 'Add to Export Queue' > XML export, with the platform auto-selecting the correct report version by subscription type. Calyx Point (article 8008) and ARIVE publish equivalent built-in MCR generation with CSV/XML export (search-level, 2026-08-20). This is the mirror image of why the MSB Call Report survives — MSBs have no equivalent dominant operational system, and the leading MSB regulatory-reporting platform (Alessa) does not produce the MSBCR at all.

rejected.name: BOI / FinCEN beneficial ownership filing artifact for small entities
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 4 — the mandate no longer exists for the intended buyer
rejected.evidence: FinCEN's own BOI page (https://www.fincen.gov/boi, fetched 2026-08-20): 'U.S. companies are exempt from the Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) reporting requirements and therefore, are no longer required to file BOI reports.' The finalized rule is dated 2026-08-11 and limits reporting to foreign entities registered to do business in a U.S. state or tribal jurisdiction. The domestic small-entity market this idea targeted was eliminated by rule nine days ago.

rejected.name: LD-2 / LD-203 lobbying disclosure report generator
rejected.killed_by: Deprioritized — free government e-filing plus no machine-readable customer input; the decisive kill check could not be completed
rejected.evidence: Scale is real and I verified it live today by curl against the keyless lda.gov REST API: https://lda.gov/api/v1/filings/?filing_year=2026&filing_period=second_quarter&filing_type=Q2 returns count 21,804 LD-2 filings for Q2 2026, and https://lda.gov/api/v1/contributions/?filing_year=2026 returns count 17,197 LD-203 contribution filings — a large recurring pool with a free public API of every prior filing, which would make roll-forward generation trivial. Two things stopped it. First, the House/Senate operate a free online filing system for LD-1/LD-2/LD-203 (https://lda.gov/system/public/, fetched 2026-08-20) that pre-populates registrant identity, and I could NOT determine whether it also copies a prior quarter's report forward — lda.congress.gov's help pages and user guide are behind a Cloudflare challenge that blocked both WebFetch and curl today, so pattern 1 is UNRESOLVED rather than cleared. Second, and independently disqualifying against the artifact-generator shape: the substantive content of an LD-2 (the specific lobbying issues, bills and agencies contacted) is not machine-readable customer data — it is the lobbyist's recollection — so there is no CSV-plus-public-corpus join, only prose drafting, which puts it on the wrong side of the engine-never-arbiter line. Quorum's LD-2 compliance module was reported at roughly $25,000/year enterprise (search-level only, 2026-08-20, not a fetched pricing page).

rejected.name: Regulation Crowdfunding Form C-AR annual report generator
rejected.killed_by: Buyer economics — the free alternative is non-compliance, and the market has already chosen it
rejected.evidence: The obligation is real (Form C-AR due within 120 days of fiscal year end, and failure to comply during the two years preceding an offering makes the issuer ineligible to use Reg CF again). But Kingscrowd's tracking (search-level, 2026-08-20) reports 47% of Reg CF companies are not reporting at all, with recent cohorts filing at 19-31%. A market where roughly half to four-fifths of the obligated population simply declines to produce the artifact, with no fine and no immediate consequence, is a market with near-zero willingness to pay for producing it faster. Colonial Stock Transfer already files crowdfunding forms as an EDGAR agent. Not proposed.

rejected.name: State unclaimed property (NAUPA II) holder report generator for banks, credit unions and insurers
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 5 (A4) plus pattern 1 — fifty jurisdictions of dormancy prose, and free state-sponsored holder software
rejected.evidence: Not proposed and not fetched-verified: dormancy periods, due dates and reportable property types are set separately by each state's unclaimed property act, which is exactly the fifty-jurisdiction prose extraction the A4 gate forbids, and multiple states pay vendors to give holders free reporting software. Listed here for completeness as an angle considered and dropped on the pattern-5 screen before spending fetches on it — no live evidence gathered, so it should be treated as an untested rejection rather than a proven one.

rejected.name: OSHA 300/300A/301 logs + March ITA electronic submission
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 — free first-party generator, spec AND API
rejected.evidence: OSHA's own injury reporting page (https://www.osha.gov/injuryreporting, fetched 2026-08-20) offers three free submission routes — manual web entry, CSV file upload for multiple establishments, and an API — plus free CSV templates and sample files for both 300A and 300/301 data, full CSV documentation, API technical specifications, job aids, video tutorials, an ITA User Guide and FAQs. OSHA has closed every gap a generator could occupy, and the 300A summary itself is column arithmetic on the 300 log. Dead on arrival.

rejected.name: EEO-1 Component 1 filing prep
rejected.killed_by: Kill patterns 1 and 3 — free EEOC portal with a published data-file upload spec, and already bundled in payroll
rejected.evidence: Jackson Lewis's 2026 employee data reporting survey (https://www.jacksonlewis.com/insights/2026-employee-data-reporting-requirements-are-employers-ready, fetched 2026-08-20) confirms EEO-1 Component 1 as an established federal filing for employers with 100+ employees and contractors with 50+, filed through EEOC's own free collection system, which publishes a data-file upload specification. The same demographic snapshot is generated by the major payroll platforms. No room for a generator.

rejected.name: California Pay Data — Payroll Employee Report (as a standalone product)
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 3 — bundled in payroll software the buyer already pays for
rejected.evidence: Greenshades (https://go.greenshades.com/blog/california-pay-data-reporting, fetched 2026-08-20) states it 'now includes a California Payroll Employee Report, generated directly from your payroll system as a downloadable .xlsx file' formatted to CRD's current reporting-year specification. Dayforce documents the same capability, Justworks supports it for PEO clients, and Affirmity and Syndio sell dedicated software above them. Only the LABOR CONTRACTOR half survives, because that data is not in the client's payroll — that is the surviving idea above.

rejected.name: DOL VETS-4212 federal contractor veteran report
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 — free filing application, free published batch-upload file spec, and a free eligibility advisor
rejected.evidence: DOL's VETS-4212 page (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/vets4212, fetched 2026-08-20) confirms the free VETS-4212 Reporting Application at vets4212.dol.gov, a free batch upload path for companies with 10+ hiring locations accepting plain text or CSV under 10MB, 'A complete description of the file format for VETS-4212 batch uploads' published inside the application, and a free elaws 'Federal Contractor Reporting Advisor'. Threshold $200,000, filing cycle August 1 to September 30. The agency ships the spec, the validator and the bulk path.

rejected.name: EPA Tier II / EPCRA Section 312 chemical inventory report
rejected.killed_by: Kill patterns 1 and 5 — EPA ships a free annual generator, and submission is fragmented across ~50 state portals
rejected.evidence: EPA's Tier2 Submit software is alive and free, not discontinued: the current version is Tier2 Submit 2025 rev 1 for reporting year 2025 (reports due March 1, 2026), it is rebuilt and republished every year, and only the current version may be used to create that year's submission file (epa.gov/epcra/tier2-submit-software and NOAA's mirror at response.restoration.noaa.gov, both surfaced 2026-08-20). EPA therefore ships exactly the artifact generator this angle would sell. The residual pain — 50 different state receiving systems, deadlines and fees — is the A4 conflict the mission forbids.

rejected.name: SDS / GHS label authoring for the 2024 Hazard Communication Standard update
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2 — a FREE incumbent, plus a crowded paid field, plus arbiter risk
rejected.evidence: UL Solutions offers self-service Safety Data Sheet authoring at no charge (https://www.ul.com/news/ul-offers-self-service-safety-data-sheet-authoring-no-charge, surfaced 2026-08-20), and paid self-serve tools already crowd the space — SDScribe from $1,595 one-time, plus SDS Manager, TotalSDS/Enhesa, ExactSDS and Quantum SDS. OSHA itself provides only QuickCards, pictograms and guidance — no generator — but that gap is already filled for free. Separately, classifying a mixture is a hazard determination the customer signs, which trips pattern 7. Note the compliance dates also moved: OSHA extended HCS compliance dates by four months, now running May 19 2026 to May 19 2028.

rejected.name: OFCCP Section 503 / VEVRAA annual Affirmative Action Program generator
rejected.killed_by: Kill patterns 4 and 1 — DOL has formally proposed to delete the computational core of the artifact, and OFCCP publishes free sample AAPs
rejected.evidence: I confirmed the mandate IS live today — 41 CFR 60-741.40(b)(1) and (b)(3) and 60-741.44 pulled from the eCFR API at the 2026-08-01 snapshot require every contractor with 50+ employees and a $50,000+ contract to prepare, maintain and annually review a written AAP per establishment — and that OFCCP has resumed 503/VEVRAA compliance evaluations with funding restored through September 30 2026. It still dies. DOL's proposed rule 'Modifications to the Regulations Implementing Section 503' (90 FR 28494, published 2025-07-01, comments closed 2025-09-02, still not final; pulled from the Federal Register API and the full text at federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2025/07/01/2025-12233.txt, fetched 2026-08-20) contains the amendatory instructions 'Sec. 60-741.45 [REMOVED AND RESERVED]' and 'Remove and reserve Sec. 60-741.45' — deleting the 7 percent utilization goal, the utilization analysis and the annual evaluation, i.e. every number in the artifact. What survives the proposal is narrative boilerplate, for which OFCCP already publishes free Sample Affirmative Action Programs (dol.gov/agencies/ofccp/compliance-assistance/sample-affirmative-action-programs). OFCCP has also kept the AAP certification portal closed, so there is no recurring must-submit event at all.

rejected.name: DOT hazmat shipping papers / dangerous-goods bill of lading generator (49 CFR 172.202)
rejected.killed_by: Kill patterns 1, 2 and 3 — free carrier and broker tools already auto-generate it
rejected.evidence: The corpus is genuinely excellent — the Hazardous Materials Table at 49 CFR 172.101 came back from the eCFR API as 2.9 MB of versioned XML at HTTP 200 on 2026-08-20 — but the artifact is already free. Freightquote's online shipping tool identifies DOT hazmat classes, auto-populates details from the UN number and generates the BOL you hand the driver (https://www.freightquote.com/blog/hazmat-shipping-safe-and-simple/, surfaced 2026-08-20); FedEx Freight and ArcBest publish their own BOL/hazmat flows; free no-signup BOL generators exist (wearewarp.com, trulos.com, bolmaker.com); and Labelmaster/DGeo DGIS occupies the paid tier. Also trips pattern 7: the shipper's certification on the paper is a legal attestation about classification and packaging.

rejected.name: FMCSA drug-and-alcohol MIS annual report (MCSA-5786)
rejected.killed_by: Kill patterns 4 and 1 — not a universal recurring duty, and free first-party submission
rejected.evidence: FMCSA's own Management Information Systems and Annual Survey Instructions pages (fmcsa.dot.gov/regulations/drug-alcohol-testing/management-information-systems-mis and /annual-survey-instructions, surfaced 2026-08-20) state that FMCSA randomly selects a group of motor carriers each year and only those notified must report, that selected carriers receive a username and password, and that submission is free online at damis.dot.gov or by hard-copy form. The premise of a universal annual filing is misstated, and the filing channel is free.

rejected.name: MSHA quarterly Form 7000-2 (Quarterly Mine Employment and Coal Production Report)
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 — free MSHA online filing, actively being expanded
rejected.evidence: MSHA's forms and online filing pages and its January 2026 announcement of a shift toward online filing of Form 7000-2 (msha.gov/compliance-and-enforcement/forms-online-filing and safetylawmatters.com/2026/01/msha-announces-shift-towards-online-filing-of-form-7000-2/, surfaced 2026-08-20) confirm free online filing available 365 days a year via MSHA eGov plus Login.gov, with a free help desk, for a form due within 15 days of each quarter's close under 30 CFR 50.30. The artifact itself is a handful of hours-and-tonnage figures — too thin to price even if the channel were open.

rejected.name: ACA 1094-C / 1095-C for small self-insured employers
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2 — live micro-SaaS at a fraction of any imaginable price
rejected.evidence: ez1095 from Halfpricesoft sells a single installation at $695.00 with UNLIMITED federal and state 1094/1095 form processing (prnewswire.com release surfaced 2026-08-20), against a field that also includes Tax1099, BoomTax, ACAwise, efileACAforms and Tax2eFile all selling self-serve 1095-C e-filing. The IRS publishes the AIR XML schema and no generator, which is the right shape — but the gap was filled years ago and is priced at flat-rate-unlimited. Separately, the input is employee and dependent SSNs, which is the PHI/PII trap the mission warns against, and the Line 14/15/16 safe-harbor coding is an arbiter decision.

rejected.name: ANGLE-LEVEL STRUCTURAL FINDING (for the factory, not an idea)
rejected.killed_by: Why mandatory workplace/safety artifacts are a graveyard for artifact generators
rejected.evidence: Across ten candidates killed live today, one law held without exception: FEDERAL WORKPLACE AND SAFETY AGENCIES SHIP FREE SUBMISSION TOOLING FOR EVERYTHING THEY COLLECT, because they want the data — OSHA ITA (CSV spec + API + templates), EEOC EEO-1, DOL VETS-4212 (batch spec + advisor), EPA Tier2 Submit (a full annual generator), MSHA eGov, FMCSA damis.dot.gov, EPA TRI-MEweb, DOL EFAST2. The complements are equally closed: anything derived from payroll is inside payroll software; anything a third party demands gets bundled by that third party (carriers generate hazmat BOLs, labs issue battery test summaries, TPAs file benefit reports); and every 'written program' has a free agency model template. The only survivors are artifacts where the DEMANDING PARTY IS DIFFUSE and the data sits OUTSIDE the customer's own systems — which is precisely why the California Labor Contractor Employee Report survived and its payroll-side twin did not. Miners on adjacent angles should test that filter first: does the agency collect it (dead), does payroll hold the data (dead), is there one third party who wants it (dead).

rejected.name: FDA Nutrition Facts / Supplement Facts panel generator from recipe data (21 CFR 101.9 / 101.36)
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 2 — live micro-SaaS incumbents far below any imagined price
rejected.evidence: ReciPal's pricing page fetched 2026-08-20 (https://www.recipal.com/pricing): Single Serving $29 USD per recipe one-time with 60 days editing and unlimited downloads; Business $59/mo ($49/mo annual) for 50 recipes/month; Business Plus $129/mo ($107/mo annual) unlimited recipes — 'all FDA/CFIA formats', self-serve, cancel anytime, free recipe on signup. A crowded field (Food Label Maker, LabelCalc, MenuSano, Nutritics) sits alongside it. The 21 CFR 101 rounding rules are indeed machine-computable, which is precisely why this was solved a decade ago. Menu labeling (21 CFR 101.11) and any FDA front-of-pack box die the same way: the same vendors ship it the week it finalises.

rejected.name: MoCRA cosmetic facility registration + product listing SPL generator (bulk SKU wedge)
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 1 — the agency ships a free generator AND free automated renewal reminders
rejected.evidence: https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products/cosmetics-direct fetched 2026-08-20 (HTTP 200 via curl; WebFetch gets 401): Cosmetics Direct 'is an FDA Structured Product Labeling (SPL) authoring tool ... that contains user friendly data entry forms, performs initial validations, creates and saves the SPL submission, and submits the SPL to FDA ... without having to use the Electronic Submissions Gateway'. Page content current as of 2026-02-11 and states that for each registered facility 'the facility contact, the FDA Direct account contact ... U.S. agent, additional contact and paper submitter ... will receive automated email reminders before the facility registration renewal date.' The companion constituent update (https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/cosmetics-news-events/fda-announces-availability-additional-submission-tools-cosmetic-product-facility-registration-and, fetched same day) adds a second free authoring tool, SPL Xforms, plus free paper Forms FDA 5066/5067. Free generator + free reminders + free fallback = nothing left to sell. The identical logic kills FDA drug listing SPL (free CDER Direct), GUDID/UDI (free web interface) and tobacco 905(i) listing (free CTP portal).

rejected.name: FSMA 204 Food Traceability Rule — traceability plan and KDE sortable-spreadsheet generator
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 4 — premise misstated against current status; no live mandate to sell against
rejected.evidence: Search 2026-08-20 across FDA and Federal Register coverage: FDA proposed a 30-month extension in March 2025, published it at https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/08/07/2025-14967/ on 2025-08-07, and the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2026 directed FDA not to enforce before 2028-07-20. The original 2026-01-20 compliance date is gone; the operative date is now July 20, 2028 — nearly two years past this factory's horizon, with cheap traceability vendors already positioning. The recurring artifact is also weak: the traceability plan is a one-time written document and the sortable spreadsheet is produced only on FDA request, not on a schedule.

rejected.name: TTB Alcohol Facts panel and major-food-allergen label generator
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 4 — no mandate exists; both rules are still proposals
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. TTB Notice No. 237 (Alcohol Facts) and Notice No. 238 (major food allergen labeling) are Notices of Proposed Rulemaking published 2025-01-17 (see https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/17/2025-00955/major-food-allergen-labeling-for-wines-distilled-spirits-and-malt-beverages); TTB extended the comment periods by 120 days to 2025-08-15 and no final rule has published. TTB's own proposal sets compliance at five years after a final rule publishes. There is no artifact anyone is obliged to produce. Separately, COLA applications are filed through TTB's free COLAs Online portal, so even the existing label-approval path is first-party free.

rejected.name: GHS Safety Data Sheet and hazard-label authoring (OSHA HazCom 2024, mixtures deadline 2027)
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 2 — cheap self-serve incumbents, including an AI one
rejected.evidence: Search 2026-08-20 returned live authoring products with published prices: SDScribe at $1,595 one-time ($2,795 with inventory/production manager, +$695 foreign language, 30-day free trial) at https://www.sdscribe.com/; ERA-EHS 'SDS Authoring Software on Demand' starting 'as low as $144.00 USD' with pay-per-SDS purchase at https://ondemand.era-ehs.com/sds; SDS Manager markets an 'AI Safety Data Sheet Creator' at https://sdsmanager.com/us/sds-authoring/; TotalSDS by Enhesa positions explicitly on undercutting authoring incumbents. On top of that, mixture classification is a liability-bearing determination (pattern 7 exposure) and OSHA publishes no classification list, so the reference corpus would have to be ECHA's EU harmonised table used by analogy — not authoritative for a US SDS.

rejected.name: US packaging EPR annual supply reports (Circular Action Alliance, six states)
rejected.killed_by: A4 conflict — the reporting spec and material lists are gated, and the artifact is a portal screen not a file; plus quote-only enterprise incumbents
rejected.evidence: https://circularactionalliance.org/producer-reporting fetched 2026-08-20 states that detailed reporting guidance goes only to producers who have completed the CAA Account Registration Form and signed the Participant Producer Agreement: 'Please complete the CAA Account Registration Form and sign the PPA in order to receive a link to detailed reporting guidance.' Nothing is publicly downloadable, so a corpus cannot refresh itself from public machine-readable sources. Holland & Knight's post-mortem of the first consolidated round (https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/07/2026-epr-reporting-lessons-learned-initial-consolidated-reporting, fetched 2026-08-20) confirms submission is through the CAA Producer Portal where 'portal screens differ by state program' — i.e. there is no file spec to generate against — and that reports demand a bespoke written methodology ('A single-line methodology is not acceptable, nor is a template methodology copied and pasted from another report'), which is arbiter work. Incumbents are enterprise and quote-gated: Packgine (https://packgine.ai/epr, fetched 2026-08-20) covers all seven US EPR states plus the EU and UK, prices 'scoped by SKU count and jurisdiction', shows no self-serve signup and only 'Book a Demo'; Assent partners with Lorax EPI on the same job. Cadence is also a single annual spike (2026 deadline was June 1).

rejected.name: UK pEPR Recyclability Assessment Methodology (RAM) assessment generator
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 1 and 2 together — a free component checker and a live paid platform, plus the legal duty does not bite until reporting year 2027
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. Ecosurety publishes a FREE RAM Component Checker (hub.ecosurety.com); Clarity sells 'RAM Assess' as a platform generating component-level RAG scores at scale (https://clarity.eco/services/ram-assess/); Valpak sells RAM consultancy (https://www.valpak.co.uk/compliance/packaging-compliance/recyclability-assessment-methodology/) and third-party per-SKU RAM validation was quoted in search at £50-£120 per SKU. GOV.UK's own page (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/assess-packaging-recyclability-recyclability-assessment-methodology-ram-2027, fetched 2026-08-20, published 1 July 2026, updated 2 July 2026) confirms the legal requirement is to 'use RAM 2027 to assess and report the recyclability of the household packaging they supply for the reporting year 1 January to 31 December 2027' — reported in 2028. The compliance-scheme channel (Valpak, Ecosurety, Comply Direct) also already bundles it for most obligated producers.

rejected.name: CPSC Children's Product Certificate / General Certificate of Conformity generator
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 2 plus a non-spec — a generator already exists and the agency says any word processor will do
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. DocAssure.ai already sells a Children's Product Certificate generator that 'creates CPSC-ready CPCs in three steps' for submission to Amazon, Shopify or distributors, auto-mapping fields from test reports (https://www.docassure.ai/children_protective_certificate_cpc/). CPSC's own guidance is that no format need be followed so long as the seven required elements from 16 CFR 1110 are present, and that a CPC is not applied for or registered — meaning Word or Google Docs is a complete substitute, and there is no file spec to be the moat.

rejected.name: USMCA certification of origin generator with tariff-shift analysis
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 2 plus pattern 7 — free templates everywhere, an existing document product, and the origin call is an arbiter decision
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. Shipping Solutions already ships USMCA certification-of-origin document creation with stored, copy-forward records and blanket 12-month certificates (https://shippingsolutionssoftware.com/blog/usmca-certificate-of-origin); freight forwarders and brokers (Livingston, AIT, usmcacertificate.com) publish free fillable templates and instructions. The only part that is not commoditised — deciding whether a good qualifies as originating under the Annex 4-B product-specific rules — is a legal determination with tariff-rate and penalty consequences that an unattended product must not sign, and it depends on HTS classification of every component, which is judgment rather than computation.

rejected.name: DSCSA EPCIS artifact product for small dispensers (Nov 27, 2026 exemption expiry)
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 3 plus a misread of who generates the artifact
rejected.evidence: FDA's exemption ends 2026-11-27 for dispensers with 25 or fewer licensed pharmacists/technicians (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-supply-chain-security-act-dscsa/exemptions-under-drug-supply-chain-security-act, surfaced 2026-08-20), so the deadline is real — but dispensers RECEIVE and store EPCIS data, they do not generate it; the generators are manufacturers, repackagers and wholesalers. And the receiving side is already served free or bundled: transaction information reaches pharmacies 'through EPCIS, EDI 856, a supplier portal, email, or another accepted method', with the big wholesalers' own portals and pharmacy management systems supplying it as part of what the pharmacy already pays for. There is no recurring artifact the small dispenser must produce.

rejected.name: PACT Act monthly state delivery reports for vape/tobacco DTC sellers
rejected.killed_by: A4 conflict across ~50 state formats, plus existing incumbents
rejected.evidence: 15 U.S.C. 376 requires a report to the tobacco tax administrator of every state shipped into 'no later than the 10th of each month' — genuinely mandatory and monthly, with misdemeanor exposure. But each state prescribes its own form and procedure (Pennsylvania REV-1163/REV-1164, Massachusetts Form CT-MM, Utah, Montana, Ohio and California each with their own filing route — all surfaced 2026-08-20), which is exactly the fifty-jurisdiction form-and-portal fleet A4 forbids. Incumbents already occupy it: Token of Trust ships a PACT Act Compliance Module that 'automates delivery reporting' (https://tokenoftrust.com/blog/the-pact-act-monthly-reporting-checklist-what-every-vape-retailer-must-file-by-june-10-2026/), Avior Tax runs vapetaxes.com, and Avalara covers the excise side.

rejected.name: FTC EnergyGuide label generator as a standalone business
rejected.killed_by: Market size, on the regulator's own arithmetic — folded into 'Basic Model' as a wedge instead of being sold alone
rejected.evidence: FTC's PRA notice 88 FR 84330 (fetched 2026-08-20) estimates label DRAFTING at 'no more than four minutes per basic model' for 25% of 69,676 basic models a year = 1,161 hours annually across the entire United States, costed at $18.97/hr data-entry labour — roughly $22,000 a year of national labour. The 112,272-hour 'labeling' line is almost entirely the physical act of affixing labels (111,111 hours at 4 seconds per unit across ~100,000,000 units shipped). A label-only product is therefore a wedge and an SEO surface, not a company. The money is in the adjacent DOE certification collection, which the same agency prices at $56,645,445 a year — which is why the proposed idea leads with the certification report and treats the label as the visible hook.

rejected.name: USMCA Certification of Origin generator (BOM + tariff-shift / RVC math from HTSUS General Note 11)
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2 — a live, self-serve, published-price micro-SaaS already sells exactly this; plus kill pattern 1-lite, free certificate generators give away the form.
rejected.evidence: Kendrick Trade LLC (© 2026) publishes self-serve pricing today at https://www.kendricktrade.com/pricing (fetched 2026-08-20): 'USMCA Qualification and Certificate Generation ... Fully qualify your Products against the usmca product specific rules of origin, generate certificates from within our portal' — $499/mo for 4,800 BOMs/yr and 6,000 certificates, $999/mo for 10,000 BOMs/yr and 14,000 certificates, free trial, 'Get started' checkout, plus a Document Solicitation line at $249.99/$499.99/$999.99 per month for supplier origin-document collection. Their product page (https://www.kendricktrade.com/, fetched 2026-08-20) confirms it reviews Bills of Material against Product Specific Rules of Origin, produces qualification worksheets, and issues certificates for a blanket period of up to 12 months — i.e. the entire imagined product including the annual recurrence. Free generators additionally give away the certificate itself: BorderBuddy 'USMCA / CUSMA Certificate of Origin Generator (Free)' (https://borderbuddy.com/cusma-usmca, HTTP 200, fetched 2026-08-20) and Zipments' USMCA certificate generator (https://www.zipments.io/tools/usmca-certificate-generator, HTTP 200, fetched 2026-08-20). Worth recording for whoever revisits this: the underlying economics ARE strong — USTR's 2026-07-28 notice puts a 10% Section 301 duty on goods of Canada and Mexico with U.S. note 52(g)/(h) exempting USMCA-originating goods via 9903.05.93/9903.05.94 (fetched 2026-08-20), and the rules-of-origin corpus is genuinely tractable: HTSUS General Note 11 downloads as a 395KB / 136-page PDF from https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/file?release=currentRelease&filename=General%20Note%2011 (fetched 2026-08-20) whose product-specific rules extract as highly regular formulaic sentences ('A change to subheading 8442.30 from any other heading ... provided there is a regional value content of not less than 60 percent where the transaction value method is used'). The math is buildable; the market is taken.

rejected.name: Section 232 steel / aluminum / copper derivative metal-content value declaration
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 4 — premise misstated vs the primary legal text. The computation was abolished four months ago.
rejected.evidence: The proclamation of 2026-04-02, published 2026-04-09 (raw text fetched today from https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/04/09/2026-06960.txt), states: 'the additional ad valorem duty imposed pursuant to section 232 on aluminum articles and aluminum derivative articles under Proclamation 9704, as amended; on steel articles and steel derivative articles under Proclamation 9705, as amended; and on copper articles and copper derivative articles under Proclamation 10962 shall apply to the full customs value of the imported product, regardless of metal content', effective 12:01 a.m. EDT on 2026-04-06, at 50% (25% for UK-origin metal content, 10% for derivative articles whose metal was melted/poured or smelted/cast in the United States). A product that computes and documents the steel/aluminum content value of a derivative article has no remaining legal function. What survives is melt-and-pour / smelt-and-cast country reporting, which is a supplier-document-collection problem — and that is precisely the job Kendrick Trade already sells at $249.99–$999.99/mo (https://www.kendricktrade.com/pricing, fetched 2026-08-20).

rejected.name: Duty drawback claim package generator (unused-merchandise / substitution, 19 U.S.C. 1313(j))
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2 — a live AI-native incumbent with an unbeatable price (contingency, $0 upfront) already occupies the SMB end; and its model has a licensed human broker in the loop, which the autonomy gates forbid us from matching.
rejected.evidence: Zollback (https://www.zollback.com/, HTTP 200, fetched 2026-08-20) markets 'AI Duty Drawback & Tariff Refund Services ... Zollback uses AI to find, calculate, and file duty drawback claims with U.S. Customs, recovering up to 99% of the import duties you've already paid. No upfront cost. You only pay when we deliver your refund', badged 'SOC 2 Type 1 Certified · ABI Certified Filer · Licensed U.S. Customs Broker', and explicitly targets the segment a subscription product would aim at: 'If your annual refund potential is under $100K, traditional providers won't take your case ... Most small and mid-size importers get nothing.' A flat subscription cannot beat $0-upfront contingency for this buyer. Zollback also states 'Our in-house licensed customs brokers review every claim before submission' — a human-in-the-loop step we could not replicate under A2/A3 and could not omit without taking on the arbiter role. (The underlying legal opportunity is real and worth noting: Section 301 duties are drawback-eligible under 19 U.S.C. 1313 and the new 10–12.5% duties of the 2026-07-28 USTR action therefore enlarge the pool — but the pool is already being fished.)

rejected.name: BIS encryption annual self-classification report generator (Supplement No. 8 to Part 742 CSV)
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 2 — a free, live, no-signup generator already emits the exact required file.
rejected.evidence: The mandate is genuine and beautifully machine-specified. 15 CFR 740.17(e)(3), fetched today from https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-01/title-15.xml?part=740&section=740.17 (HTTP 200, 35,653 bytes; title 15 up_to_date_as_of 2026-08-18), requires the annual report to be 'received by BIS and the ENC Encryption Request Coordinator no later than February 1 the following year', emailed to crypt-supp8@bis.doc.gov and enc@nsa.gov, 'as an electronic file in comma separated values format (.csv) adhering to the specifications set forth in paragraph (b) of supplement no. 8 to part 742'; Supplement No. 8 (fetched today from the same API, part 742) fixes twelve exact column headers ('PRODUCT NAME, MODEL NUMBER, MANUFACTURER, ECCN, AUTHORIZATION TYPE, ITEM TYPE, SUBMITTER NAME, TELEPHONE NUMBER, E-MAIL ADDRESS, MAILING ADDRESS, NON-U.S. COMPONENTS, NON-U.S. MANUFACTURING LOCATIONS'), controlled vocabularies of 5 ECCNs, 2 authorization types and 49 item types, 50/250-character limits and a no-embedded-comma rule. But https://annual-self-classification-report.github.io/ (HTTP 200, 61,320 bytes, fetched 2026-08-20) is a free, live, no-signup, no-affiliation web tool that 'only helps to generate correct formatted CSV files as required per Supp. 8 to Part 742', ships a sample report AND an App Store Connect example, and runs entirely client-side. The artifact is already generated for free. The adjacent semi-annual sales report under 740.17(e)(1) is not covered by that tool, but it applies only to items classified under (b)(2)/(b)(3)(iii) — i.e. holders of a BIS CCATS, who already have compliance staff — and the regulation prescribes no strict format ('Recommended file formats ... include spreadsheets, tabular text or structured text'), so there is no spec-defined artifact to generate deterministically.

rejected.name: FinCEN Residential Real Estate Report (RRER) batch-XML generator for title and settlement agents
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 4 — the mandate no longer exists. The rule took effect 2026-03-01 and was vacated 18 days later.
rejected.evidence: FinCEN's own Residential Real Estate Rule page states verbatim: 'On March 19, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas issued an order vacating the Residential Real Estate Rule', that FinCEN 'in conjunction with the Department of Justice, has appealed the decision', and that under the court's order 'reporting persons are not required to file Real Estate Reports with FinCEN and are not subject to liability if they fail to do so' (https://www.fincen.gov/rre and https://www.fincen.gov/rre-newsroom, both fetched 2026-08-20). The batch spec is still live — Technical-Specifications-Batch.pdf returns HTTP 200, 1,304,159 bytes (curl, 2026-08-20) — and a micro-SaaS (fincenreportready.com, HTTP 200 2026-08-20) already exists for it, which makes the vacatur the whole story: a fully-specified, machine-readable artifact with zero legal obligation behind it.

rejected.name: Construction lien waiver + preliminary notice generator (deadline math by state, statutory waiver forms)
rejected.killed_by: Kill patterns 1 and 2 — the category leader gives the document generation away free, and kill pattern 5 on top (50-state statutory deadline prose).
rejected.evidence: Levelset (acquired by Procore) offers a free account with 'free lien forms, lien waiver forms, and notice forms', charging only for the physical send at '$59/recipient' for notices and demands, with lien filing behind a sales-gated subscription (https://www.levelset.com/pricing/, fetched 2026-08-20). rejected.name: AIA G702/G703 pay application package generator for subcontractors
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 4 — there is no legal mandate, only a contract term, so no agency publishes a spec; compounded by AIA's copyright in the forms themselves.

The monthly pay application is imposed by the prime contract, which means the 'spec' is whatever each GC's accounting department wants. Rejected before spending fetches on Siteline/Flexbase pricing, because even a proven price gap would sit on top of a non-mandate and a copyright.

rejected.name: NYC Local Law 97 annual building emissions report generator
rejected.killed_by: Kill pattern 1 (the city already ingests the data and computes) plus kill pattern 7 (the report must be certified by a Registered Design Professional, so an unattended product cannot sign the artifact).

rejected.name: EUDR due diligence statement (DDS) generator for SME operators via TRACES
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 4 — premise misstated against the current legal position. The SME mandate has been pushed out and structurally gutted: SMEs are largely no longer the filer, and where they are, the artifact is one-off rather than recurring.
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. Application deferred to 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and 30 June 2027 for micro and small — beyond a build horizon. Worse for the shape: responsibility to submit a DDS now sits solely with the operator who FIRST places the product on the EU market, not with downstream traders or processors, removing most SMEs from the filing population altogether; and micro/small primary operators in low-risk countries submit a single simplified one-time declaration rather than repeated DDS submissions. A one-off declaration by a shrunken population is not a recurring artifact. Sources surfaced: https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation and https://eudr-navigator.com/deadlines (search-surfaced 2026-08-20, not individually rendered — flagged, but the rejection rests on the deferral and the first-placer scoping, both consistently reported).

rejected.name: Companies House software-only accounts filing (iXBRL) for micro-entities from 1 April 2027
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 2 — live micro-SaaS incumbents at a fraction of any imaginable price, including free tiers, plus a first-party approved-software list that does the discovery for the buyer.
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. Paid filing software for small and dormant companies already starts at around £20 per year, and free options exist — some providers offer free accounts filing for micro-entities outright. A market where the incumbent floor is £20/year and zero cannot support a new entrant. Sources surfaced 2026-08-20: https://tinytax.co.uk/guides/companies-house-software-filing and https://tinytax.co.uk/guides/companies-house-webfiling-closing (search-surfaced; pricing figures are the vendors' own comparison claims, not independently rendered — but the existence of free micro-entity filing is sufficient to kill regardless of the exact floor).

rejected.name: DORA Register of Information (xBRL-CSV) generator for small EU financial entities
rejected.killed_by: Patterns 1 and 2 together — the regulator publishes free official templates and there is already a free third-party validator, plus 2026 proportionality lets unchanged entities skip a full submission.
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. The ESAs publish the 15 official templates set by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956, the applicable validation rules and a visual data model as free resources; the official EBA template is free to download with no cost and no email required. A free validator already runs at https://www.doravalidator.com/ (Arendt), and free Excel templates are circulating (https://vendorica.com/templates/dora/register-of-information/). On top of that, the 2026 cycle is explicitly more proportionate than 2025: entities with no material change can confirm their situation is unchanged rather than resubmit, subject to NCA instruction. Free spec plus free validator plus a shrinking submission population is not a market.

rejected.name: EFRAG VSME sustainability report generator for SME suppliers
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 1 — EFRAG itself ships a free Digital Template with auto-calculations and consistency checks AND a free open-source XBRL converter. Compounded by pattern 4: the standard is a Commission Recommendation, not a filing mandate on SMEs.
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. EFRAG publishes a free VSME Digital Template implemented in MS Excel with interactive elements, auto-calculations, consistency checks and direct links to the standard's text, plus a free and open-source Digital Template to XBRL converter; the taxonomy package and Digital Template v1.2.0 were published 27 February 2026 and the template now ships in multiple languages. Resources at https://www.efrag.org/en/vsme-digital-template-and-xbrl-taxonomy and https://xbrl.efrag.org/downloads/vsme/. Status: VSME was released December 2024 and endorsed by the Commission as a Recommendation adopted 30 July 2025 — a recommendation for non-listed SMEs, not a duty with a filer, a deadline and a penalty. The agency has already built and given away the exact product.

rejected.name: UK MTD for Income Tax quarterly submission tool
rejected.killed_by: Patterns 1, 2 and 3 — HMRC runs a first-party software finder, free products exist, and the job is bundled into accounting suites the buyer already pays for.
rejected.evidence: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-software-thats-compatible-with-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax (fetched 2026-08-20, page last updated 13 July 2026) states that all listed software has been through HMRC's recognition process, directs users to HMRC's own software finder tool, and confirms that 'free products are available for those with simple tax affairs'. HMRC itself curates the market and free options are in it — the category is closed to a new self-serve entrant.

rejected.name: UK Plastic Packaging Tax quarterly return and tax-account generator
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 3 bundling plus an unviably small buyer population — the packaging compliance schemes that already handle these customers' EPR obligations sell PPT as an attached service to the same accounts.
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. HMRC records 4,927 businesses registered for the tax as of August 2025 — a market roughly half the size of the payment practices population, and the registration threshold (10 tonnes of plastic packaging manufactured or imported in a 12-month period) is what defines it. The rate rose to £228.82 per tonne from 1 April 2026. Existing packaging compliance schemes already sell PPT services into exactly this customer base alongside EPR (e.g. https://www.beyond.ly/services/plastic-packaging-tax/, surfaced 2026-08-20). Flagged as a softer reject than the others: the bundling evidence is a vendor service page surfaced in search rather than a fetched price, and the TAM figure is HMRC's, reported secondhand. It fails on size and attachment risk rather than on a clean pattern hit.

rejected.name: UK GPSR responsible-person product-safety documentation for non-EU sellers
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 4 (shape) plus pattern 7 — the EU GPSR imposes no recurring, spec-defined, machine-readable artifact that anyone files on a schedule; its only EU submission is the incident-driven Safety Business Gateway notification, and the substantive deliverable (a risk assessment / technical file) is a judgment about product safety that an unattended engine must never author.
rejected.evidence: Rejected on shape without a fetch, and recorded as such rather than dressed up with a source. There is no periodic GPSR return, no published field spec, and no filing deadline — so there is nothing for a deterministic generator to produce. Anything a product could generate here would be a safety judgment the customer signs, which is exactly the engine-never-arbiter line. No live verification was performed today and none should be inferred; this is a shape rejection, not an evidenced one.

rejected.name: UK Employment Related Securities (ERS) annual return generator
rejected.killed_by: Pattern 3 — the return is generated inside the cap-table and share-scheme platforms the buyer already pays for, and HMRC publishes the ODS templates itself.
rejected.evidence: Searched 2026-08-20. The obligation is real and recurring (annual online return by 6 July following the tax year, £100 automatic penalty, further £300 at three and six months, £10/day after nine months — https://www.gov.uk/guidance/employment-related-securities-bulletin-65-april-2026 and firm commentary surfaced 2026-08-20). But the population that has reportable events overwhelmingly runs a cap-table or option-scheme platform that produces the return, and HMRC supplies the submission templates. No competitor pricing was found either, so the willingness-to-pay case is unproven on both sides. Dropped in favour of hardening one idea rather than carrying a second soft one.
